Subject: Re: Capacity question — holiday spikes and billing

Hi Olga,

We had an unexpected 4x spike during the holiday weekend (Black Friday weekend) that ate through our burst headroom and triggered significant overrun charges. Ops attached a short CSV with per-hour token volumes for the week (FastRetail_peak_report_Q4.csv).

Before we get into a formal renewal conversation, procurement asked me to confirm what flexible commercial options Redwood offers for unpredictable spikes — specifically:
- A short-term quota increase (one-off) instead of permanent commit changes
- A pre-paid/retainer model for elastic headroom that can be used across months
- How overrun true-ups are calculated and whether we can amortize those costs across a quarter

We run retail campaigns where brief, high-intensity bursts are normal. For budgeting, it would help to avoid surprise bills and have a predictable mechanism (even if it costs more upfront).

Can you outline options and a rough estimate for a 6–8 hour 4x spike event that we saw? Also include what the time-to-activate is for any standby capacity.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Gupta
Head of Platform Reliability, FastRetail

Hi Samir — thanks for the details and for sending the per-hour CSV. I reviewed the spike pattern with our SRE and pricing teams.

Short summary of options tailored to FastRetail:

1) Elastic Headroom Subscription (recommended for your profile)
   - Monthly retainer that reserves a pool of burst capacity you can draw from on demand.
   - Unused headroom does not roll over month-to-month, but we offer a 30% credit back toward subsequent month for planned events (requires 72-hour notice).
   - Standby activation: standard is < 24 hours for staged capacity; guaranteed 6–12 hour activation SLAs available with a higher retainer.

2) One-off temporary quota uplift
   - Short-term quota increase for pre-approved dates (48–72 hour lead time typical). This is priced at the prevailing commit rate for the increased tier and billed upfront or on the next invoice.

3) Post-event reconciliation / amortized true-up (your ask)
   - We can amortize an overrun across up to 3 subsequent invoices (quarterly amortization) if a minimum Elastic Headroom Subscription (one-month retainer) is in place.
   - Overrun rate for amortized reconciliation is discounted relative to on-demand overrun — our proposal: 60% of on-demand token price if amortized over 3 invoices.

Example (very rough): your reported 4x peak would have produced an incremental 1.2M tokens of overrun. If billed on-demand, that would be $9,000; with a 3-month amortized path under Elastic Headroom + true-up, the up-front retainer is $1,200/mo and the amortized overrun charge would be $1,800 (60% of $3,000) split across 3 invoices = $600/mo for 3 months.

I attached a short spreadsheet with the example math and two commercial options (elastic_headroom_pricing_v1.xlsx).

Next steps I recommend:
- If you want guaranteed activation within 12 hours, that requires the upgraded standby SLA and a signed addendum (we can generate a draft).
- If procurement prefers amortization, we can include amortization language and the 60% discounted overrun rate in the SOW.

Marissa from Commercial will follow up with an official quote and a sample amortization term sheet. CC'd.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Elastic Headroom commercial terms & example amortization

Hi Samir — following up with a concise commercial proposal and an attached worksheet that breaks out the math (elastic_headroom_pricing_v1.xlsx). Key points below so procurement can consume quickly: 

- Product: Elastic Headroom Subscription (EH-Standard)
  - Monthly retainer: $1,200
  - Standby activation SLA: 24 hours standard; 12-hour guaranteed (EH-Priority, additional $1,000/mo)
  - Retainer credit: 30% credit toward planned events if requested with 72-hour notice

- Overrun / True-up mechanics (amortized option)
  - If EH-Standard is active, overrun can be amortized across up to 3 invoices (quarters not allowed; 3 sequential monthly invoices).
  - Amortized overrun rate: 60% of on-demand overrun price (applies only to token consumption above committed allowances).
  - Minimum amortization trigger: single overrun event > 800k tokens or cumulative > 1.5M tokens in a rolling 30-day window.

- Example (numbers from the CSV you provided):
  - Reported incremental tokens: ~1.2M
  - On-demand overrun cost estimate: $9,000
  - Amortized cost at 60%: $5,400 split across 3 invoices = $1,800 / month for 3 months
  - With EH-Standard retainer ($1,200/mo), total incremental monthly impact = $3,000 for 3 months (first month includes retainer + first amortized slice).

Operational next steps we can include in the SOW: PO -> addendum for EH -> activation window documented -> amortization clause and sample amortization schedule attached. Please note: amortization requires signing the EH subscription before the final invoice for the event is issued (we won’t retroactively amortize if the subscription is not active by invoice date).

I attached the pricing worksheet. If procurement wants a different amortization horizon or a different discount, we can run a scenario — larger discounts available for longer retainer commitments or annualized EH subscriptions.

Samir — would you like me to prepare a formal quote & SOW for legal/finance to review? If so, please confirm billing contact and target PO date.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
